original_question: How large are the contributions of time-odd mean-field components induced by the time evolution of the mean field to the collective mass in large-amplitude collective motion, and how can those effects be evaluated reliably within modern nuclear energy density functionals rather than being omitted as they are in the usual cranking mass?
target_in_paper: Evaluate the contributions of the time-odd components of the mean field (which break time-reversal invariance) induced by the time evolution of the self-consistent mean field to the collective mass (inertial function) in microscopic calculations of large-amplitude collective motion, and to what extent these effects can be evaluated using energy density functionals currently under active development, in contrast to their omission in the conventional cranking mass.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies: 1) the focus on time-odd mean-field components induced by the time evolution of the mean field; 2) their contribution to the collective mass (inertial function) in large-amplitude collective motion; 3) the omission of these effects in the traditional cranking mass; and 4) the need to evaluate them reliably within modern nuclear energy density functionals.
missing_details: Specify that the cranking mass is obtained via adiabatic perturbation theory (ATDHFB) and ignores time-odd induced effects (Belyaev [28], Baranger and Vénéroni [31]).
Highlight that the ASCC collective mass includes time-odd effects by solving the moving-frame QRPA equations (equations (6) and (7)).
Mention that it is unclear to what extent time-odd effects enter the GCM-GOA mass with real generator coordinates.
Define “time-odd mean-field components” explicitly as those breaking time-reversal symmetry (e.g., currents and spin densities in EDFs).
Clarify that the energy density functionals of interest include modern Skyrme, Gogny, or covariant EDFs under active development.
Define the collective mass as the inverse of B(q) appearing in the collective Hamiltonian H(q,p)=V(q)+½B(q)p².
State that the open problem remains to microscopically evaluate these effects using EDFs currently under development.
Specify the context of large-amplitude collective motion: e.g., quadrupole shape dynamics and shape coexistence/mixing phenomena at zero temperature.
refined_question: How significant are the contributions of time-odd mean-field components (those breaking time-reversal symmetry) induced by the time evolution of the self-consistent mean field to the inertial function B(q) in microscopic calculations of large-amplitude collective motion, and how can these contributions be microscopically evaluated using modern nuclear energy density functionals (such as Skyrme, Gogny, or covariant EDFs) within frameworks like the ASCC method or GCM-GOA, in contrast to their omission in the conventional cranking (ATDHFB) mass?
justification: The refined question remains narrowly scoped to the statement in section 6.1 of the paper, explicitly names the time-odd components and their role in collective mass calculations, contrasts the ASCC and cranking masses, and specifies the use of modern EDFs for reliable evaluation, fully incorporating the paper’s intent.
